To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in the newborn lamb, the AT1 receptor plays a role in the control of both resting blood pressure, and renal vascular resistance.
AT1 receptors are involved in the control of systemic and renal hemodynamic parameters in conscious lambs aged ∣ 1 and ∣ 6 weeks of age.

the AT1 receptor antagonists, ZD 7165, but not the AT2 receptor, PD 123 319, decreased renal vascular resistance and increased renal blood flow, and decreased mean arterial pressure in conscious lambs at doses ≥400 μg kg−1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of ANG II in the regulation of renal blood flow and systemic blood pressure.
the role of the angiotensin receptor subtypes in the regulation of renal and systemic hemodynamics in the developing lamb.
the development of the cardiovascular and renal systems in newborn animals, and the role of the renin-angiotensin system (RAS) in these developmental processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AT1 receptor is involved in the regulation of resting blood pressure in the newborn and that the AT2 receptor has no detectable effect on resting blood pressure or RVR in the newborn.

the effects of ANG II on blood pressure and renal vascular resistance are mediated through the AT1 receptor and are not modulated by AT2 receptor activation in conscious lambs aged ∣1 and ∣6 weeks of life.
AT1 but not the AT2 receptor mediates the effects of ANG II on systemic and renal blood flow and pressure in the newborn animal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AT1 receptors mediate the effects of ANG II on blood pressure, RBF, and RVR, but that AT2 receptors are not involved in the regulation of these parameters in newborn and young sheep.
the AT2 receptor is not involved in the regulation of blood pressure and renal hemodynamics under physiological conditions.
the AT1 receptor is a major regulator of blood pressure, renal perfusion pressure, and renal function in newborn animals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AT1 receptors play an important role in the maintenance of blood pressure and in the regulation of RVR during the early postnatal period.
the AT1 receptor is the primary target for ANG II in newborn animals.
the AT1 receptor is the main mediator of ANG II effects on blood pressure and renal function in newborn animals.
